steps.label: 1 · Era still (candidate 2 of 3)
steps.prompt:
Redraw this shot as a 1930s hand-drawn animation pencil test on a single sheet of warm off-white animation paper.
Soft graphite linework with confident, expressive contours over faint light-blue construction lines and loose circles.
The characters are fully drawn; the background is indicated with lighter, simpler layout lines.
Monochrome only: graphite and faint blue pencil on paper. Keep the characters readable through silhouette and values:
Bram's coat is shaded darker with graphite, Pip's raincoat lighter, and Bram's knitted scarf is left as clean white paper with a few knit lines.
Three small round registration peg holes along the bottom edge of the paper. No scratches, dirt, sepia or film grain.

Keep exactly the same camera, framing, composition and character positions as the first image.
The characters are Bram, a tall, sturdy lamplighter with a charcoal flat cap, brown hair, a big round nose, rosy cheeks, a thick curled handlebar moustache, a long deep-red wool coat with brass buttons and flap pockets over a dark sweater, a long cream knitted scarf with fringed ends wrapped around his neck with one end hanging down his chest, and dark trousers; and Pip, a small child about half Bram's height with auburn hair, wearing a yellow sou'wester rain hat, a yellow duffle raincoat with dark toggles, black trousers and teal rain boots.
Preserve their silhouettes, proportions, relative heights, costumes, poses and expressions.
Bram stands in the middle facing us; Pip stands just outside the arched doorway to the right of him.
Keep the setting: a night street: a warm plaster wall with an arched doorway and a green door, a glowing wall lamp above the door, a dark red brick wall on the left, a black iron street lantern in the right foreground, and a clock tower against the dark blue night sky behind.
Do not add characters, props, text, captions, logos, borders or watermarks.

The second image shows Bram up close and the third image shows Pip up close, for identity only.
inputs: Frame-zero render of the Lens & Framing lab, HD cast (24 mm, t = 2.40 s) + close-up crops of Bram and Pip

steps.label: 2 · Draft clip from the approved still (take a; 2 takes: b colorized the pencil test)
steps.prompt:
A 1930s graphite pencil-test animation. The whole shot stays a monochrome pencil drawing on warm off-white paper from the first frame to the last: grey graphite lines and light blue construction lines only, never any color, paint or fill. The drawings change on every second frame; the paper and the background drawing stay still. One continuous six-second shot with a completely fixed camera: no zoom, pan or cuts.
0-1s: Bram, the tall lamplighter in the red coat, stands still by the glowing doorway; Pip, the small child in the yellow raincoat, has just stepped out beside the door.
1-2s: Bram hears something and his eyes and head turn toward Pip.
2-4s: Bram turns his body toward Pip and waves back, raising his right hand in front of him; Pip waves eagerly with one arm out to the side.
4-6s: Pip gives a small happy hop and both settle into warm, delighted expressions. Bram's scarf end sways slightly with his turn and settles; it stays wrapped around his neck.
Keep the same art style, character designs, proportions and background throughout. Clear anticipation, readable silhouettes.
No new characters, no text, no dialogue, no music.
